newsitem.title: UK: Imperial confident in its legal defences.
newsitem.headline: Imperial confident in its legal defences.

text.p: British-based Imperial Tobacco Ltd, about to be demerged from Anglo-U.S. basic industries congomerate Hanson Plc, said on Friday it was confident its legal defences would resist any health claims made against it.
It made the comments in a statement issued after a London law firm said it would launch a group action against Imperial and U.S.-owned Gallaher on behalf of some 40 cancer sufferers.
"Imperial has strong defences against such cases and will defend them vigorously. We are confident we will win any such speculative cases brought against us," it said.
The firm said it was aware that legal aid boards in both England and Scotland had declined to support out of public funds cases claiming that smoking has caused ill health.
"In the hundreds of cases which have been brought against tobacco companies worldwide none have lead to any payment of damages," Imperial added.
A few cases in the U.S. have resulted in some liability being found against tobacco companies but these have been appealed or are due to be appealed.
Analysts told Reuters that they felt the new UK action, and the "no-win, no fee" approach by the lawyers, raised the risk level from litigation to companies in active here like Imperial.
